summary: At barely 0.7 square miles, Benton Park packs roughly 8,100 people per square mile into a footprint smaller than many shopping malls — making it one of the denser pockets in inland Southern California's San Bernardino County, wedged into the flat, sun-baked grid of the greater San Bernardino metro. That density shows up not as high-rises but as tightly spaced single-family homes and small apartment buildings lining compact blocks, where nearly everything is technically walkable by distance even if the streetscape itself is more utilitarian than charming. The affordability numbers look striking on paper — a median home value around $230,600 against a median household income of roughly $62,500 gives a price-to-income ratio near 3.7, far below coastal California norms — but a poverty rate of 32.8% signals that a significant share of households faces real financial pressure, and median rent at $1,190 still claims a meaningful fraction of that median income. The climate is relentlessly sunny, averaging 9.7 hours of daylight-driven warmth with highs around 81°F year-round, which means summer afternoons push well past that average into genuinely hot territory while winters stay mild. Employment skews toward logistics, healthcare, and service-sector work concentrated across the broader Inland Empire, so most commutes radiate outward along I-215 or I-10 corridors. Benton Park is a place where the math of homeownership technically works in a state where it often doesn't, but the tradeoff is an inland, infrastructure-lean setting where the savings reflect the surroundings.
